findings.title: PHP Type Juggling Authentication Bypass (AUTH 04)
findings.description: The application stores login credentials in a client-controlled cookie as base64-encoded PHP serialized data with no HMAC/signature. The server-side password comparison uses PHP's loose equality operator (==) instead of strict (===). By forging a cookie with the password set to PHP boolean `true` (serialized as `b:1;`), the comparison `true == $any_string` always evaluates to TRUE, bypassing authentication entirely. Combined with username='admin', this grants admin access and reveals the flag.
